system_prompt:
You are a principal solution architect at a top-tier consulting firm.

Analyse the provided Business Requirement Document and/or Technical Documentation carefully. Extract EVERYTHING relevant and produce a complete architecture JSON.

NOTES:
- Either BRD and/or Technical Documentation may be provided (at least one will be present)
- If only Technical Documentation is provided, infer the project requirements and solution from it
- If only BRD is provided, design a reasonable architecture based on the requirements
- If both are provided, synthesize both perspectives

CRITICAL RULES:
- Return ONLY valid, complete JSON — no markdown, no explanation, no truncation
- Every string value: max 20 words, clear and specific
- NO empty arrays — every array must have real content derived from the input
- alignment.goals: exactly 5 specific goals (extracted from BRD or inferred from tech doc)
- alignment.success_metrics: exactly 5 measurable KPIs
- problem_statement.current_pain_points: exactly 5-6 specific pains
- proposed_solution.key_differentiators: exactly 5 specific technical differentiators
- data_flow: exactly 6-8 sequential steps describing the actual system data flow
- architecture.components: exactly 6-8 components, each with id, label, name, role, technology fields
- architecture.connections: directed edges between component ids for the diagram
- technology_stack: fill ALL 6 layers with real tech names from the input (frontend/backend/ai_ml/data/infrastructure/security)
- non_functional: fill all 5 fields (scalability/security/availability/performance/compliance) with specific statements
- roadmap: exactly 3 phases, each with exactly 4 concrete deliverables
- risks: exactly 4-5 risks each with specific mitigation
- assumptions: exactly 4-5 specific assumptions
- open_questions: exactly 4-5 specific open questions

IMPORTANT for architecture.components — each component MUST have ALL these fields:
  "id": snake_case unique identifier (e.g. "fastapi_backend")
  "label": short display name (e.g. "FastAPI Backend")
  "name": full descriptive name (e.g. "FastAPI REST Backend Service")
  "role": one-line description of what it does (e.g. "Handles all API requests and orchestrates pipeline")
  "technology": specific tech used (e.g. "FastAPI, Python, Pydantic, Uvicorn")

OUTPUT FORMAT:
{
  "project": { "name": "", "tagline": "", "client_context": "" },
  "alignment": { "goals": [], "business_value": "", "success_metrics": [] },
  "problem_statement": { "current_pain_points": [], "impact": "", "root_cause": "" },
  "proposed_solution": { "summary": "", "key_differentiators": [], "approach": "" },
  "architecture": {
    "pattern": "", "frontend": "", "backend": "", "ai_layer": "", "data_store": "", "hosting": "",
    "components": [
      { "id": "user_client", "label": "User / Client", "name": "Web Browser / API Client", "role": "Entry point for all user interactions", "technology": "Web Browser, REST client" }
    ],
    "connections": [
      { "from": "user_client", "to": "frontend", "label": "HTTPS" }
    ]
  },
  "data_flow": [],
  "technology_stack": { "frontend": [], "backend": [], "ai_ml": [], "data": [], "infrastructure": [], "security": [] },
  "non_functional": { "scalability": "", "security": "", "availability": "", "performance": "", "compliance": "" },
  "roadmap": [
    { "phase": "Phase 1 - Foundation", "duration": "Weeks 1-4", "deliverables": [] },
    { "phase": "Phase 2 - Core Build", "duration": "Weeks 5-10", "deliverables": [] },
    { "phase": "Phase 3 - Scale & Optimise", "duration": "Weeks 11-16", "deliverables": [] }
  ],
  "risks": [{ "risk": "", "mitigation": "" }],
  "assumptions": [],
  "open_questions": []
}

project.name: ShopEase E-Commerce Platform
project.tagline: Unified web and mobile commerce platform with real-time SAP ERP integration
project.client_context: Retail enterprise migrating 8,000 SKUs from SAP ERP to a scalable omnichannel platform supporting 50,000 concurrent peak users

goals: Launch fully integrated web and mobile ShopEase platform within 6 months of kickoff
Migrate 8,000 existing SKUs from SAP ERP and scale catalog to 25,000 SKUs
Sustain 50,000 concurrent users during peak events with sub-3-second page loads
Synchronize SAP ERP stock levels to storefront within seconds of any inventory change
Deliver daily, weekly, monthly sales reports filterable by region, category, and vendor
alignment.business_value: Eliminates lost revenue from absent digital channel, enables peak-event monetization, and unifies vendor, regional, and admin operations on one platform
success_metrics: Platform live with 8,000 SKUs migrated within 6 months of project kickoff
Page load time under 3 seconds at 50,000 concurrent users during peak load tests
SAP ERP inventory sync latency under 5 seconds for 99th percentile of updates
Zero stock discrepancy errors reported across all active SKUs post-launch
Admin sales reports generated and filterable within 10 seconds across all dimensions

current_pain_points: No centralized digital sales channel causes direct revenue loss during high-traffic events like Diwali
Real-time inventory visibility absent, leading to stock discrepancy errors across 8,000 SKUs
No pricing control or customer behavior analytics prevents data-driven commercial decisions
Fragmented operations across vendors, regional store teams, and central admin with no unified system
Existing infrastructure cannot scale to 50,000 concurrent users or onboard new vendors efficiently
No automated logistics coordination with shipping partners Delhivery and BlueDart
problem_statement.impact: Revenue leakage during peak sale events, operational inefficiency across all stakeholder groups, and inability to scale vendor and SKU growth
problem_statement.root_cause: Absence of a unified digital commerce platform; all operations siloed within SAP ERP with no customer-facing or vendor-facing digital layer

proposed_solution.summary: Cloud-native omnichannel e-commerce platform with real-time SAP ERP sync, role-based portals for all personas, and integrated payments and logistics
key_differentiators: Real-time bidirectional SAP ERP integration for sub-5-second inventory sync across all storefronts
Horizontally scalable microservices architecture sustaining 50,000 concurrent users under peak load
Unified role-based access layer serving customers, vendors, regional managers, and central admins
Native multi-payment gateway support including UPI, net banking, cards, and Bajaj Finance EMI
Automated logistics orchestration with Delhivery and BlueDart via event-driven integration layer
proposed_solution.approach: Microservices backend deployed on cloud infrastructure, React web and React Native mobile frontends, event-driven SAP ERP sync via middleware, and CDN-accelerated storefront delivery

architecture.pattern: Microservices with event-driven integration, API Gateway, CDN-accelerated frontend, and real-time ERP sync middleware
architecture.frontend: React.js (Web), React Native (Mobile), Next.js SSR for storefront SEO and performance
architecture.backend: Node.js / Java Spring Boot microservices behind API Gateway with Redis caching
architecture.ai_layer: Product recommendation engine, customer behavior analytics, and demand forecasting service
architecture.hosting: AWS (EKS for containers, CloudFront CDN, RDS, ElastiCache, S3)

components.label: User / Client
components.name: Web Browser and Mobile App Client
components.role: Entry point for customers, vendors, regional managers, and admins
components.technology: React.js, Next.js, React Native, Web Browser

components.label: CDN & Edge
components.name: Content Delivery Network and Edge Cache
components.role: Serves static assets and cached pages globally for sub-3-second load times
components.technology: AWS CloudFront, Edge Locations, S3 Static Hosting

components.label: API Gateway
components.name: Unified API Gateway and Auth Layer
components.role: Routes all client requests, enforces RBAC, rate limiting, and JWT validation
components.technology: AWS API Gateway, Kong, OAuth2, JWT

components.label: Core Microservices
components.name: Core Business Logic Microservices Cluster
components.role: Handles catalog, orders, inventory, users, payments, and vendor management domains
components.technology: Node.js, Java Spring Boot, Docker, Kubernetes (EKS)

components.label: ERP Integration
components.name: SAP ERP Integration and Sync Middleware
components.role: Bidirectional real-time sync of inventory and SKU data between SAP ERP and platform
components.technology: Apache Kafka, MuleSoft, SAP BAPI/RFC, REST Adapters

components.label: Payments & Logistics
components.name: Payment Gateway and Logistics Integration Layer
components.role: Processes UPI, cards, net banking, Bajaj EMI, and coordinates Delhivery and BlueDart
components.technology: Razorpay, Bajaj Finance API, Delhivery API, BlueDart API, Webhooks

components.label: Data Platform
components.name: Transactional and Analytical Data Platform
components.role: Stores product catalog, orders, sessions, and powers analytics and search

components.label: Admin & Analytics
components.name: Admin Dashboard and Sales Analytics Service
components.role: Delivers filterable daily, weekly, monthly reports by region, category, and vendor
components.technology: React.js, ClickHouse, Apache Superset, REST APIs

data_flow: Customer or vendor accesses ShopEase via React web or React Native mobile app over HTTPS
CloudFront CDN serves cached static assets and SSR pages; cache misses forwarded to API Gateway
API Gateway validates JWT token, enforces RBAC role, applies rate limiting, and routes to microservice
Core microservice processes request (catalog browse, order placement, inventory update, vendor upload)
Inventory or catalog change triggers Kafka event consumed by SAP ERP Integration Middleware
MuleSoft middleware syncs stock delta to SAP ERP and pushes confirmed update back to PostgreSQL and Redis cache
Payment requests routed to Razorpay or Bajaj Finance API; confirmed orders trigger Delhivery or BlueDart shipment creation
All transactional events streamed to ClickHouse; Admin Dashboard queries ClickHouse for real-time filterable sales reports

non_functional.scalability: Kubernetes HPA scales microservices pods horizontally to sustain 50,000 concurrent users; catalog scales to 25,000 SKUs without schema changes
non_functional.security: PCI-DSS compliant payment processing, JWT-based RBAC across all five personas, AWS WAF, TLS 1.3 encryption in transit and at rest
non_functional.availability: 99.9% uptime SLA with multi-AZ AWS deployment, automated failover for RDS, and health-check-driven pod restarts on EKS
non_functional.performance: All storefront pages load within 3 seconds at peak load via CloudFront CDN caching and Redis session/catalog caching layer
non_functional.compliance: PCI-DSS Level 1 for payment data, GDPR-aligned data handling for customer PII, SAP ERP audit trail preserved for all inventory sync events

deliverables: Cloud infrastructure provisioned on AWS with EKS, RDS, ElastiCache, and CloudFront configured
SAP ERP integration middleware deployed with Kafka pipeline and initial 8,000 SKU migration completed
Authentication service with RBAC implemented for all five user personas
CI/CD pipelines established with Terraform IaC and automated environment promotion
Customer-facing web and mobile storefront launched with catalog browse, search, and cart functionality
Order management, payment gateway (UPI, cards, Bajaj EMI), and Delhivery/BlueDart logistics integrated
Vendor portal deployed for catalog management, inventory updates, and order visibility
Admin dashboard live with daily, weekly, monthly sales reports filterable by region, category, and vendor
Load testing at 50,000 concurrent users completed with performance tuning and CDN cache optimization
Product recommendation engine and customer behavior analytics deployed and integrated into storefront
Regional store manager interface delivered with regional inventory and sales visibility features
Security audit, PCI-DSS compliance validation, and full UAT sign-off completed before go-live

risks.risk: SAP ERP integration complexity causes delays in real-time inventory sync delivery
risks.mitigation: Engage SAP-certified integration specialists early; use MuleSoft pre-built SAP connectors and run parallel sync testing from Week 2

risks.risk: Peak load of 50,000 concurrent users causes performance degradation or downtime
risks.mitigation: Conduct staged load testing from Week 10 using AWS Load Testing tools; implement auto-scaling policies and CloudFront cache warming before peak events

risks.risk: PCI-DSS compliance gaps in payment processing delay go-live approval
risks.mitigation: Engage PCI-DSS QSA auditor in Phase 2; use Razorpay hosted payment fields to minimize card data scope on platform

risks.risk: Vendor onboarding adoption is slow, limiting catalog growth beyond 8,000 SKUs
risks.mitigation: Deliver intuitive vendor portal with bulk CSV upload, onboarding documentation, and dedicated vendor support during Phase 3 rollout

risks.risk: Data migration errors during 8,000 SKU transfer from SAP ERP corrupt catalog integrity
risks.mitigation: Execute migration in dry-run mode with automated reconciliation scripts validating SKU count, pricing, and stock levels before cutover

assumptions: SAP ERP system exposes stable BAPI/RFC or REST APIs sufficient for real-time bidirectional inventory synchronization
Bajaj Finance, Delhivery, and BlueDart provide sandbox API environments available from project Week 3 for integration development
Client provides clean, validated SKU master data export from SAP ERP for the initial 8,000 SKU migration
Peak concurrent user target of 50,000 refers to simultaneous active sessions, not total daily unique visitors
Client's central admin team will define report filter taxonomies (region hierarchy, category structure) by end of Week 2
open_questions: Which specific frontend frameworks does the client prefer for web and mobile, or is framework selection delegated to the architecture team?
What is the acceptable SAP ERP downtime window for integration middleware deployment and initial SKU migration cutover?
Should the recommendation engine be built in-house or leverage a managed service such as AWS Personalize or Google Recommendations AI?
Are there existing vendor contracts with Razorpay or another payment aggregator, or does the client require a new payment gateway evaluation?
What data residency or sovereignty requirements apply to customer PII and transaction data stored on AWS infrastructure?
